components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; min-height:44px; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:8px 16px; border:1px solid var(--hc-border, #e0e2dc); border-radius:8px; background:var(--hc-surface, #fff); color:var(--hc-text, #282828); font:700 16px/1.2 'Helvetica Neue',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif; text-decoration:none; transition:background-color 160ms ease,border-color 160ms ease,color 160ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--hc-accent, #f8d651) 5%, #fff); border-color:var(--hc-accent-text, #725a00); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--hc-accent, #f8d651); outline-offset:3px; }

narrative.overview:
The site should feel like a well-run operating system made visible: calm at first glance, specific on inspection, and structured around the decisions a client needs to make. The hierarchy comes from typography, proportion, spacing, and real evidence rather than a stack of decorative cards.

The visual system pairs a near-white canvas with light editorial surfaces and a deliberately scarce gold accent. It rejects generic developer portfolios, resume framing, AI-agency futurism, glossy generated imagery, full-site dark premium-tech styling, and excess cards or dividers.
keyCharacteristics: Proof-led and operational rather than promotional.
Spacious, direct, and easy to scan without feeling sparse.
Flat by default, with elevation reserved for controls, navigation, and real artifacts.
One obvious primary action per decision surface.
Responsive layouts that preserve reading comfort and content priority.

rules.name: The Gold Means Action Rule
rules.body: CTA Gold is reserved for directional cues, focus, and meaningful selection; controls stay light rather than using yellow fills.

rules.name: The Editorial Surface Rule
rules.body: Editorial charcoal is reserved for embedded demos or status panels; site chrome and page surfaces stay light.

rules.name: The Read Before Display Rule
rules.body: Long-form pages use the Article Title scale, and body copy controls the reading measure; display typography must not dominate the article.

rules.name: The Shared Editorial Column Rule
rules.body: Set the 75ch measure on the shared header and main-content wrappers at body-text scale. Let the title, deck, article, and author section fill that same physical column; do not apply ch directly to the title.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If color, spacing, or content hierarchy already establishes the boundary, do not add a border or shadow.

dos: Do reserve #f8d651 CTA Gold for directional cues, focus, and meaningful selection states; keep controls light.
Do use spacing and typographic hierarchy before reaching for borders, rules, or cards.
Do show real artifacts, outcomes, constraints, and working details as evidence.
Do use one shared 75ch editorial column for blog metadata, title, deck, article, and author content.
Do preserve keyboard access, visible focus, reduced-motion behavior, and WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.
donts: Don't build a generic developer or creative portfolio organized around personal taste instead of client problems.
Don't use employment or resume framing that makes the site read like a job application.
Don't use AI agency hype, futuristic claims, or unsupported promises.
Don't use glossy generated imagery in place of real artifacts and evidence.
Don't use full-site dark premium-tech styling that obscures reading and proof.
Don't use excess cards, dividers, horizontal rules, or decorative containers to manufacture hierarchy.
Don't constrain blog titles with a character-based max-width or scale them beyond the Article Title token.
